reading.body:
Squire Patton Boggs filed 34 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI, with Tata Consultancy Services and the American Staffing Association accounting for 21 of them.

The client list is the useful signal. Two of the six named clients are Indian or Indian-linked IT services bodies, Tata Consultancy Services and Nasscom, and a third, SK Americas, is the US arm of a Korean conglomerate. Vertiv is a data center infrastructure company. This is not a roster of AI model developers. It is a roster of firms that build, staff, and cool the physical layer that AI runs on, plus the outsourcing industry that supplies the labor around it.

The lobbyist counts show a firm spreading work widely rather than concentrating it. David Schnittger appears on 16 of the 34 filings, and no other individual appears on more than 11. Sixteen named lobbyists appear on one to five filings each. That pattern is consistent with a large firm assigning many hands to a broad portfolio rather than a small team running one campaign.

The data does not say what any of these clients argued for. A filing reports that a firm lobbied on an issue, not the position it took, so the direction of the advocacy is not recoverable here. It also does not cover spending amounts, the specific bills named, or any activity outside the LDA reports this site has collected.

summary: SQUIRE PATTON BOGGS filed 34 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 30906.
